modelAnswer: Quaid-e-Azam Muhammad Ali Jinnah stands as a great leader for Muslims and the world through his visionary establishment of Pakistan based on the Two-Nation Theory and his commitment to democratic principles. He founded the All India Muslim League, led the Pakistan Movement, and secured a homeland where Muslims could practice their faith freely. His legacy extends beyond Muslims as he championed democracy, equality, tolerance, and social justice, principles enshrined in the Objectives Resolution of 1949, which he moved as first Prime Minister. Jinnah's secular vision for a modern Islamic state, combined with his advocacy for fundamental rights and constitutional governance, made him a beacon for nations seeking to balance religious identity with democratic values. His famous address to the Constituent Assembly, emphasizing that citizens of all faiths would have equal rights, demonstrated his universal humanitarian outlook. The Quaid's leadership transformed the political consciousness of Muslims and inspired movements for self-determination globally, proving that principled leadership transcends religious and geographical boundaries. His constitutional framework, based on sovereignty of Allah, democracy, and justice, continues to guide Pakistan and serves as a model for Islamic democracies worldwide.
